I get that this is an unpopular view but:

We need more journalists & fewer pundits.

We need more original reporting & fewer hot takes riffing off the news.

We don't have

My take on the @hasanthehun stuff:

- Dem politicians have long been happy to tout themselves talking to controversial far-right fascists to flaunt their left-punching credentials and they’ve concurrently tried to starve all left-leaning media of attention, so the whole fake “controversy” here just spotlights that deeper asymmetry (and to be clear I’m not equating Hasan with the far right, nor am I weighing in on all his views/statements/declarations — I’m making a larger indisputable point)

-

Reporters doing accountability journalism are getting mowed down by mass layoffs & are now almost extinct — while the targets of their accountability reporting are giving hundreds of millions of dollars to pundits. 

What stage of the media dystopia is this?

"[Sean Duffy] lobbied for... American, Delta and United, the three largest airlines in the country," says @wjm-air.bsky.social on @levernews.com. 

"Sean Duffy, the guy who is in charge of all of this, was a lobbyist for the industry that does not want to be regulated," adds David Sirota.

People who don't want this kind of thing reported hate journalism & loathe the idea of politicians being held accountable. They should be understood as fans who think politics is merely an entertaining game in which they should root for their team, rather than a thing that has real-life stakes.

In the mind of wild-eyed partisan liberals who care about literally nothing, simply pointing out that a legislator is touting a surveillance pricing bill that she refuses to support in her own legislature is considered a horrific "attack" rather than simply "journalism."
